title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #16

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these plants lives for many years? (1 mark)
   A. Sukuma wiki grown for one season
   B. Mango tree
   C. Maize
   D. Beans

2. What can you use to draw and label a plant if you have a computer at school? (1 mark)
   A. A ruler only
   B. A calculator only
   C. A stopwatch
   D. A drawing app

3. What are the two main types of things carried by the stem? (1 mark)
   A. Water and food
   B. Sound and light
   C. Air and stones
   D. Heat and cold

4. Which of these animals gives birth to live young? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Frog
   C. Housefly
   D. Goat

5. How do young mammals get their first food? (1 mark)
   A. By eating grass
   B. By eating stones
   C. By drinking their mother's milk
   D. By hunting

6. What do fish use to take oxygen from water? (1 mark)
   A. Gills
   B. Feathers
   C. Horns
   D. Lungs

7. Which of these is NOT an animal? (1 mark)
   A. A tilapia
   B. A wooden toy horse
   C. A cow
   D. A housefly

8. How many legs does a spider have? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Eight
   C. Four
   D. Ten

9. Which group of vertebrates has feathers? (1 mark)
   A. Reptiles
   B. Birds
   C. Fish
   D. Amphibians

10. Why is it important to protect wild animals and their homes? (1 mark)
   A. They can be sold cheaply
   B. They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
   C. They do not need food
   D. They are dangerous to all people

11. Which of these helps to keep teeth healthy? (1 mark)
   A. Eating many sweets
   B. Brushing twice a day
   C. Biting hard objects
   D. Never visiting a dentist

12. What can help a child with diarrhoea while waiting to see a health worker? (1 mark)
   A. Eating only sweets
   B. Eating unwashed fruit
   C. Drinking dirty water
   D. Drinking clean water and ORS as advised

13. What does the gullet do? (1 mark)
   A. Pushes swallowed food to the stomach
   B. Makes saliva
   C. Stores faeces
   D. Absorbs food into blood

14. Which of these is true about the small intestine? (1 mark)
   A. It stores faeces
   B. It swallows food
   C. Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
   D. It chews food

15. What is saliva? (1 mark)
   A. A type of waste
   B. A tube in the stomach
   C. A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   D. A germ

16. Which of these is a healthy habit for digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Never washing fruits
   B. Eating food that fell in dirt
   C. Washing hands before eating
   D. Drinking water from a dirty pond

17. How many millilitres are in 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 10 000
   B. 1000
   C. 100
   D. 10

18. What instrument measures the volume of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Measuring jug
   C. Stopwatch
   D. Beam balance

19. What is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Anything that is hot
   B. Anything that makes sound
   C. Anything that shines
   D. Anything that has mass and takes up space

20. A pupil wants to make a toy car from waste. Which materials are suitable? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel and leaves
   B. Fire and paper
   C. Water and air
   D. A box and bottle tops

21. Why are rotting waste heaps a health danger? (1 mark)
   A. They make water sweet
   B. They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   C. They cool the air
   D. They make soil red

22. Which of these is non-decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Egg shells
   B. Banana peel
   C. Tin can
   D. Leaves

23. Which of these can be made from waste for the classroom? (1 mark)
   A. A car engine
   B. A new mountain
   C. A house
   D. A dustbin

24. Which item is a paper waste that can be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. Old newspapers
   B. Banana peel
   C. Plastic bottle
   D. Glass bottle

25. In a school, who could check that bins are emptied and clean? (1 mark)
   A. Only the wind
   B. Nobody
   C. Class monitors
   D. Only the visitors

26. Which of these is an example of a place where water may be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. A dry shamba
   B. A tap
   C. A road
   D. A water treatment plant

27. Why is a bucket better than a running tap for washing a bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. It uses more water
   B. It makes the bicycle dirty
   C. It uses less water
   D. It makes it heavier

28. What is rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Drinking rainwater from puddles
   B. Digging wells
   C. Selling rainwater
   D. Catching and storing rainwater

29. Which of these can change the shape of dough? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to it
   B. Looking at it
   C. Leaving it alone
   D. Pressing with a force

30. Which force is at work when you pour water and it flows down a slope? (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Light
   C. Magnetism only
   D. Gravity

31. A cyclist presses the brakes and slows down. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Increases speed
   B. Holds objects together
   C. Decreases speed
   D. Starts motion

32. Which force acts on a ball thrown into the air and brings it back down? (1 mark)
   A. Friction
   B. Sound
   C. Gravity
   D. Light

33. How can a farmer keep a wheelbarrow running smoothly? (1 mark)
   A. Add sand to the wheel
   B. Leave it in the rain
   C. Use rough paint
   D. Oil its moving joints

34. Which of these can be a cheap way of lighting a house in a rural area? (1 mark)
   A. Many electric heaters
   B. Solar lamp
   C. Hundreds of candles
   D. A big generator

35. What do reflectors on a road or bicycle do? (1 mark)
   A. Make their own light all night
   B. Shine when car lights fall on them
   C. Make sound
   D. Make heat

36. Which of these is a safe practice with light? (1 mark)
   A. Never look straight at the sun
   B. Stare at bright lights
   C. Shine torches in eyes
   D. Look at the sun with your eyes

37. Which of these is a safety rule about the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Shine a mirror in eyes
   B. Go out at midday without shade
   C. Look at it for a long time
   D. Never look directly at it

38. Which of these materials passes heat quickly? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Metal
   C. Wood
   D. Dry cloth

39. Which is a correct statement about heat? (1 mark)
   A. It moves from cold to warm
   B. It has mass
   C. It stays still
   D. It moves from a warm object to a cooler one

40. Why is a thermometer better than touching to find how hot something is? (1 mark)
   A. It is heavy
   B. It is noisy
   C. It is dangerous
   D. It is safe and gives a number

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how windows, roofs and walls can be used to make a house brighter by day. (4 marks)

42. Describe how a poster can teach the community about water conservation. Give four features. (4 marks)

43. State the difference between mass and volume. (2 marks)

44. Describe the function of each part of the digestive system: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. (5 marks)

45. Explain why rubbing your hands makes them warm. (2 marks)

46. A school tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much water is lost in a school day of 8 hours and in 5 school days? (3 marks)

47. Give three examples where a force holds objects together. (3 marks)

48. Explain why burning waste is not a good way of managing waste and give better methods. (5 marks)

49. Give three uses of friction in daily life. (3 marks)

50. A family of five uses a tap that drips 1 litre every hour. Calculate how much water is wasted in one week and suggest what they should do. (5 marks)

51. State three things a child should do when he has diarrhoea. (3 marks)

52. Explain the dangers of diarrhoea and what should be done to help someone who has it. (5 marks)

53. Sort into decomposable and non-decomposable: egg shells, tin can, cotton cloth, polythene bag, cow dung, glass bottle. (4 marks)

54. Explain how a frog is similar to and different from a fish. (4 marks)

55. A pupil wants to find out which material is transparent, translucent or opaque. Describe a test. (4 marks)

56. Explain how wasting water can affect other people and the family. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Mango tree
   Mango trees live for many years, while beans and maize live for one season.

2. D — A drawing app
   A drawing app can be used to draw and label plant parts.

3. A — Water and food
   The stem carries water and mineral salts up and food made in leaves to other parts.

4. D — Goat
   Goats are mammals and give birth to live young. Hens, frogs and flies lay eggs.

5. C — By drinking their mother's milk
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

6. A — Gills
   Fish breathe using gills.

7. B — A wooden toy horse
   A toy is not alive. It does not feed, grow or reproduce.

8. B — Eight
   Spiders have eight legs.

9. B — Birds
   Only birds have feathers.

10. B — They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
   Wild animals are part of our environment and bring income through tourism.

11. B — Brushing twice a day
   Brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

12. D — Drinking clean water and ORS as advised
   Water and ORS replace what the body loses.

13. A — Pushes swallowed food to the stomach
   The gullet squeezes food down.

14. C — Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
   Absorption takes place there.

15. C — A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   Saliva wets food and starts to digest starchy foods.

16. C — Washing hands before eating
   Clean hands prevent germs from entering the mouth.

17. B — 1000
   1 litre is 1000 ml.

18. B — Measuring jug
   A measuring jug or cylinder shows volume.

19. D — Anything that has mass and takes up space
   Matter has mass and occupies space.

20. D — A box and bottle tops
   A box and bottle tops make a toy car.

21. B — They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   Flies and rats carry germs.

22. C — Tin can
   Metal does not rot easily.

23. D — A dustbin
   A dustbin can be made from waste materials like a bucket or box.

24. A — Old newspapers
   Paper can be turned into new paper.

25. C — Class monitors
   Monitors can share the responsibility.

26. D — A water treatment plant
   Treatment plants clean used water.

27. C — It uses less water
   A bucket has a limited amount of water.

28. D — Catching and storing rainwater
   Harvesting means collecting rainwater from roofs.

29. D — Pressing with a force
   A force can squeeze and stretch dough.

30. D — Gravity
   Gravity pulls water downhill.

31. C — Decreases speed
   Brakes use friction to slow the bicycle.

32. C — Gravity
   Gravity pulls the ball to the ground.

33. D — Oil its moving joints
   Oil reduces friction.

34. B — Solar lamp
   Solar lamps use free energy from the sun.

35. B — Shine when car lights fall on them
   Reflectors bounce light back.

36. A — Never look straight at the sun
   Looking at the sun harms eyes.

37. D — Never look directly at it
   The sun can harm eyes.

38. B — Metal
   Metals pass heat easily.

39. D — It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

40. D — It is safe and gives a number
   A thermometer avoids burns and measures.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Large windows let in light, translucent roof sheets let in light, light-coloured walls reflect light, open curtains.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A clear message, big pictures, short slogan, bright colours, ideas for saving water, placed where many people see it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four features.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and volume is the space it takes up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Mouth: chews and adds saliva. Gullet: pushes food down. Stomach: churns with juices. Small intestine: finishes digestion and absorbs food. Large intestine: takes back water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rubbing causes friction and friction produces heat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for friction and 1 mark for heat.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 16 litres in one day and 80 litres in five days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 x 8, 1 mark for 16, 1 mark for 16 x 5 = 80.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Glue holding paper, nails holding wood, rope tying things, stitches holding cloth, screws.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Burning gives harmful smoke, especially from plastic. Better: reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and use bins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for better methods.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brakes, shoes gripping the ground, lighting matches, rough tyres, sharpening tools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: 24 x 7 = 168 litres. They should repair the tap or ask an adult or plumber to fix it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 24 hours, 1 mark for 24 x 7, 1 mark for 168, 1 mark for fixing the tap, 1 mark for units.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tell an adult, drink clean water or ORS, and see a health worker. Keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: The body loses water quickly and the person becomes weak, especially young children. They should drink clean water and ORS, rest, see a health worker and keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 3 marks for actions.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: egg shells, cotton cloth, cow dung. Non-decomposable: tin can, polythene bag, glass bottle.
   Working / marking points: Award 4 marks for all correct, 3 for five, 2 for four and 1 for three.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both are vertebrates and have a backbone. A frog has moist skin and lives on land and in water, and a fish lives in water and has gills and fins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for similarity and 2 marks for differences.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a torch in a dark room. Put tissue paper, clear plastic and a book one at a time between the torch and a wall. Record whether all, some or no light passes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equipment, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for classification.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Less water is left for others, especially in dry areas. The family pays more for water and may have to fetch more.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for others and 2 marks for family.
